short: Micro-ECoG closed-set word decoding (M05, M06) departs from 2009 intracortical formant decoding and clinical grids but stays standard: one patient, one split, selection on test data.
position: The paper [@kellis2010decoding] changes two components, both standard: each departs from the single prior speech decoder but is shown in one patient on one split. Its sensors (M05) use 1-mm micro-ECoG where earlier intracranial speech recordings used clinical grids or depth electrodes (2 of 3 prior experiments, Appendix); its decoder (M06) classifies a closed word set where the one prior decoder regressed formants. The strongest confound is selection on the evaluation data: trials were kept only if judged stereotyped, more than half discarded for some words (Sec. 2.2), and the best five FMC electrodes, ranked by overall accuracy with no separate selection set described (Sec. 2.6, 3.3; inference), carry gains of up to 20.0 percentage points. That micro-scale recording matters is untested: the clinical grid in the same patient was not decoded (Sec. 2.1, 2.3).
